lines: The girl holds firm: not promised.
After a deer, with no guide —
The noble one sees early: better to let go.
Holding firm in small things: good.

notes.name_en: 屯 （說文： 屯難也，象艸木之初生） is a sprout forcing the ground; it also means gather/store/garrison (active in 'setting up lords' and L5's stored fat). Title takes the sprout as primary, gathering as overtone.
notes.judgment: 元亨利貞勿用有攸往利建侯。 Despite comma-per-word punctuation in the base text, 勿用有攸往 is read as one phrase ('do not set out anywhere'); read as separate items it contradicts L1's staying. 建侯 = setting up lords as helpers.
notes.image: 雲雷屯；君子以經綸。 Upper water as cloud over lower thunder. 經綸 kept as its concrete craft — sorting warp threads — not Legge's government gloss.
notes.L1: 初九 磐桓。 Binome for hesitant circling, kept literal with 磐 'great rock' rather than abstract 'difficulty in advancing'. 利居貞 per glossary.
notes.L2: 六二 屯如邅如乘馬班如。匪寇婚媾女子貞不字十年乃字。 班如 refrain fixed as 'horses wheeling back' in L2/L4/L6. 字 read as betrothal ('promised'), matching 婚媾； the alternative 'bear a child' is rejected — the scene is a marriage party, not a birth. 女子 = the girl.
notes.L3: 六三 既鹿無虞惟入于林中君子幾不如舍往吝。 虞 is the forester/gamekeeper who guides the hunt — 'guide' keeps function without the office title. 幾 read as seeing the incipient turn early; 舍 （捨） = let go of the chase.
notes.L5: 九五 屯其膏小貞吉大貞凶。 Here 屯 takes its store-up sense: 膏 fat/richness hoarded, not spread. 'Fat' kept literal. 小/大貞 supplied with 'things' as grammar only.
